My wheat-maize rotation is the backbone of everything. Those two crops cover most of my land — I know them well and they give me a reliable income. My wife and her brother both work jobs off the farm, so I can't spread myself too thin. I manage the field work mostly myself with some seasonal hired labor.

For wheat this winter, I'll put in about 100 mu, using an improved variety — Jimai 22 or whatever the local agricultural station recommends this year. I always apply base fertilizer before sowing and top-dress at jointing. I irrigate at least 3 times: before sowing, at jointing, and at heading. After wheat harvest in June I immediately sow maize on the same land, no-till, straight into the stubble. Everyone around here does it that way now to save time. Hybrid maize — Zhengdan 958 is what I've used before, maybe try Xianyu 335 if the seed shop has a good deal.

For the other 63 mu of cash crops, I keep 20 mu in cotton — prices have been okay and I know it. Watermelon brings decent money, 15 mu is enough to manage without too much trouble. Chili and broccoli I keep small — 10 and 8 mu — because they need a lot of labor and attention. Stevia is the newest thing I'm doing, only 10 mu, I started a couple years back through a contract arrangement, so I'll keep that going.

I water everything from the well. Cotton and watermelon need the most irrigation. Cotton also needs the most pesticide spraying — aphids and bollworm are bad every year. I'm not going to cut corners on that.
